title.zh: 卷四八 補列傳第四十 外戚
title.raw: 卷四八 補列傳第四十 外戚 Volume 48 Biographies 40: Imperial Affines

sentences.zh: 仁自兩漢以來，外戚之家罕有全者，其傾覆之跡，逆亂之機，皆詳諸前史。

translations.literal: Since the Two Han dynasties, few households of imperial affines have been preserved intact; the traces of their ruin and the occasions of rebellion and disorder are all set forth in detail in the earlier histories.
translations.idiomatic: Since the Han dynasties, few consort clans have survived unscathed—their falls and the seeds of rebellion are fully recorded in earlier histories.

sentences.zh: 齊氏后妃之族，多自保全，唯胡長仁以譖訴貽禍，斛律光以地勢被戮，俱非女謁盛衰之所致也。

translations.literal: Among the clans of Qi consorts and empresses, many preserved themselves; only Hu Changren suffered disaster through slander and accusation, and Hulu Guang was executed because of his territorial power—neither was caused by the rise and fall of women’s influence at court.
translations.idiomatic: Among Northern Qi empresses’ kin, many kept themselves safe; only Hu Changren fell to denunciation, and Hulu Guang was killed for his territorial power—neither owed simply to the waxing and waning of palace women.

sentences.zh: 今依前代史官，述《外戚》云爾。

translations.literal: Now, following the historians of former ages, I set forth the “Imperial Affines” as follows.
translations.idiomatic: Following earlier historians, I here present the account of Imperial Affines.

sentences.zh: 趙猛，太安狄那人。

translations.literal: Zhao Meng was a native of Di in Tai’an.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Meng was from Di in Tai’an.

sentences.zh: 姊為文穆皇帝繼室，生趙郡王琛。

translations.literal: His elder sister was the successor consort of Emperor Wenmu and bore Prince of Zhao Commandery Chen.
translations.idiomatic: His elder sister was Emperor Wenmu’s successor consort and bore Zhao Commandery Prince Chen.

sentences.zh: 猛性方直，頗有器幹。

translations.literal: Meng was upright by nature and possessed considerable ability.
translations.idiomatic: Meng was upright and capable.

sentences.zh: 高祖舉義，遷南營州刺史，卒。

translations.literal: When Emperor Gaozu raised the righteous standard, Meng was transferred to be Inspector of South Ying Province and died in office.
translations.idiomatic: When Gaozu rose in arms, Meng was made inspector of South Ying Province, where he died in office.

sentences.zh: 婁叡，字佛仁，武明皇後兄子也。

translations.literal: Lou Rui, courtesy name Foren, was a nephew of Empress Wuming.
translations.idiomatic: Lou Rui, styled Foren, was a nephew of Empress Wuming.

sentences.zh: 父壯，魏南部尚書。

translations.literal: His father Zhuang was Minister of the Southern Department in Wei.
translations.idiomatic: His father Zhuang served Wei as Minister of the Southern Department.

sentences.zh: 叡少好弓馬，有武幹，為高祖帳內都督。

translations.literal: Rui in youth loved bow and horse, had martial ability, and served as a commander in Gaozu’s personal guard.
translations.idiomatic: In youth Rui loved archery and horsemanship, showed martial talent, and served in Gaozu’s personal guard.

sentences.zh: 從破尒朱於韓陵，累遷開府儀同、驃騎大將軍。

translations.literal: He followed in the defeat of the Erzhu at Hanling and was repeatedly promoted to Director of the Bureau of Ceremonial Parallels and General of Cavalry with Rapid Steeds.
translations.idiomatic: He fought at Hanling in the defeat of the Erzhu and rose through the ranks to Director of the Bureau of Ceremonial Parallels and General of Cavalry with Rapid Steeds.

sentences.zh: 叡無器幹，唯以外戚貴幸，而縱情財色，為時論所鄙。

translations.literal: Rui lacked ability and relied solely on his status as an imperial affine for favor; he indulged wealth and women and was despised by contemporary opinion.
translations.idiomatic: Rui had little talent and owed his rank only to kinship with the throne; he squandered himself on wealth and women, and contemporaries held him in contempt.

sentences.zh: 皇建初，封東安王。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Huangjian era, he was enfeoffed as Prince of Dong’an.
translations.idiomatic: At the opening of Huangjian he was made Prince of Dong’an.

sentences.zh: 高歸彥反於冀州，詔叡往平之。

translations.literal: When Gao Guiyan rebelled in Ji Province, an edict ordered Rui to go and pacify him.
translations.idiomatic: When Gao Guiyan rebelled in Ji Province, Rui was ordered to suppress him.

sentences.zh: 還，拜司徒公。

translations.literal: On his return he was appointed Director of the Department of State.
translations.idiomatic: On his return he was appointed director of the Department of State.

sentences.zh: 周兵寇東關，叡率軍赴援，頻戰有功，擒周將楊檦等。

translations.literal: When Zhou forces raided the eastern passes, Rui led troops to relieve them, fought repeatedly with merit, and captured the Zhou general Yang Biao and others.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhou troops threatened the eastern passes, Rui marched to their relief, won repeated victories, and captured the Zhou general Yang Biao and others.

sentences.zh: 進大司馬，出總偏師，赴懸瓠。

translations.literal: He was advanced to Grand Marshal and went out to command a detached force at Xuanhu.
translations.idiomatic: Promoted to grand marshal, he took a detached command at Xuanhu.

sentences.zh: 叡在豫境，留停百餘日，侵削官私，專行非法，坐免官。

translations.literal: Rui remained in the Yu region more than a hundred days, encroaching on public and private property and acting lawlessly on his own authority; for this he was removed from office.
translations.idiomatic: Rui lingered in Yu more than a hundred days, plundering public and private goods and acting with impunity, until he was dismissed.

sentences.zh: 尋授太尉。

translations.literal: Shortly afterward he was appointed Grand Commandant.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon appointed grand commandant.

sentences.zh: 薨。

translations.literal: He died.
translations.idiomatic: He died in office.

sentences.zh: 尒朱文暢，榮第四子也。

translations.literal: Erzhu Wenchang was the fourth son of Rong.
translations.idiomatic: Erzhu Wenchang was Erzhu Rong’s fourth son.

sentences.zh: 初封昌樂王。

translations.literal: He was first enfeoffed as Prince of Changle.
translations.idiomatic: He was first enfeoffed prince of Changle.

sentences.zh: 其姊魏孝莊皇後，及四胡敗滅，高祖納之，待其家甚厚，文暢由是拜肆州刺史。

translations.literal: His elder sister was Empress of Emperor Xiaozhuang of Wei; after the four Erzhu were destroyed, Gaozu took her in marriage and treated her family very generously, and Wenchang was therefore appointed Inspector of Si Province.
translations.idiomatic: His sister had been Empress Xiaozhuang of Wei; after the Erzhu were overthrown, Gaozu married her and treated her kin lavishly, and Wenchang became inspector of Si Province.

sentences.zh: 家富於財，招致賓客，既籍門地，窮極豪侈，與丞相司馬任胄、主簿李世林、都督鄭仲禮、房子遠等深相愛狎，外示杯酒之交，而潛謀逆亂。

translations.literal: His household was rich in wealth and he gathered guests; relying on his lineage, he pursued luxury to the utmost. With the chief minister’s aide Ren Zhou, registrar Li Shilin, commander Zheng Zhongli, and Fang Ziyuan he was deeply intimate—outwardly they showed the friendship of wine cups, yet secretly they plotted rebellion.
translations.idiomatic: Rich and hospitable, he leaned on his birth to live in extreme splendor. With Ren Zhou, Li Shilin, Zheng Zhongli, and Fang Ziyuan he feigned convivial friendship while secretly plotting revolt.

sentences.zh: 自魏氏舊俗，以正月十五日夜為打竹簇之戲，有能中者，即時賞帛。

translations.literal: By the old custom of Wei, on the night of the fifteenth day of the first month there was a game of striking bamboo clusters; whoever hit the mark received silk rewards on the spot.
translations.idiomatic: By Wei custom, on the fifteenth night of the first month people played at striking bamboo targets; a hit won silk on the spot.

sentences.zh: 任胄令仲禮藏刀於袴中，因高祖臨觀，謀為竊發，事捷之後，共奉文暢為主。

translations.literal: Ren Zhou had Zhongli hide a knife in his trousers; when Gaozu came to watch, they planned a sudden attack, and if the affair succeeded they would together install Wenchang as ruler.
translations.idiomatic: Ren Zhou hid a blade in Zhongli’s trousers; when Gaozu came to watch, they meant to strike—and if they succeeded, to set Wenchang on the throne.

sentences.zh: 為任氏家客薛季孝告高祖，問皆具伏。

translations.literal: A retainer of the Ren household, Xue Jixiao, informed Gaozu; on interrogation all confessed.
translations.idiomatic: Ren’s retainer Xue Jixiao exposed them to Gaozu, and under questioning all confessed.

sentences.zh: 以其姊寵故，止坐文暢一房。

translations.literal: Because of his sister’s favor, punishment was limited to Wenchang’s household alone.
translations.idiomatic: Thanks to his sister’s favor, only Wenchang’s own household was punished.

sentences.zh: 弟文略，以兄文羅卒無後，襲梁郡王。

translations.literal: His younger brother Wenlüe, because his elder brother Wenluo died without heirs, inherited the title Prince of Liang Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Younger brother Wenlüe inherited the Liang Commandery princedom when Wenluo died heirless.

sentences.zh: 以文暢事，當從坐，高祖特加寬貸。

translations.literal: Because of Wenchang’s affair he should have been punished as an associate, but Gaozu specially granted him leniency.
translations.idiomatic: He should have shared Wenchang’s guilt, but Gaozu spared him.

sentences.zh: 文略聰明儁爽，多所通習。

translations.literal: Wenlüe was clever, sharp, and widely accomplished in many arts.
translations.idiomatic: Wenlüe was brilliant, quick-witted, and accomplished in many arts.

sentences.zh: 世宗嘗令章永興於馬上彈胡琵琶，奏十餘曲，試使文略寫之，遂得其八。

translations.literal: Emperor Shizong once had Zhang Yongxing play the foreign pipa on horseback and perform more than ten pieces; he had Wenlüe transcribe them, and Wenlüe got eight correct.
translations.idiomatic: Shizong once had Zhang Yongxing play the pipa on horseback through more than ten pieces and asked Wenlüe to write them down; he caught eight.

sentences.zh: 世宗戲之曰：「聰明人多不老壽，梁郡其慎之。

translations.literal: The emperor jested, “Clever men often do not live long; Prince of Liang, take care.”
translations.idiomatic: The emperor teased him: “Clever men seldom live long—take care, Prince of Liang.”

sentences.zh: 」文略對曰：「命之修短，皆在明公。

translations.literal: Wenlüe replied, “Whether life is long or short is all in Your Majesty’s hands.”
translations.idiomatic: Wenlüe answered, “Long life or short is entirely for Your Majesty to decide.”

sentences.zh: 」世宗愴然曰：「此不足慮也。

translations.literal: The emperor said sadly, “That is nothing to worry over.”
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, moved, “That is nothing to worry about.”

sentences.zh: 」初，高祖遺令恕文略十死，恃此益橫，多所淩忽。

translations.literal: Earlier, Gaozu’s testament had pardoned Wenlüe ten capital offenses; relying on this he grew ever more overbearing and often insulted others.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu’s will had granted Wenlüe ten stays of execution; emboldened, he grew ever more insolent.

sentences.zh: 平秦王有七百里馬，文略敵以好婢，賭而取之。

translations.literal: The Prince of Pingqin owned a horse worth seven hundred li; Wenlüe matched it against a fine maidservant, gambled, and won it.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Pingqin owned a horse said to run seven hundred li in a day; Wenlüe wagered a fine maid against it and won.

sentences.zh: 明日，平秦致請，文略殺馬及婢，以二銀器盛婢頭馬肉而遺之。

translations.literal: The next day the Prince of Pingqin came to redeem the stake; Wenlüe killed the horse and the maid and sent him the maid’s head and the horse’s flesh in two silver vessels.
translations.idiomatic: When Pingqin came to claim his stake, Wenlüe slaughtered horse and maid and sent back their flesh and her head in silver dishes.

sentences.zh: 平秦王訴之於文宣，系於京畿獄。

translations.literal: The Prince of Pingqin complained to Emperor Wenxuan, and Wenlüe was imprisoned in the capital jail.
translations.idiomatic: Pingqin appealed to Wenxuan, and Wenlüe was thrown into the metropolitan prison.

sentences.zh: 文略彈琵琶，吹橫笛，謠詠，倦極便臥唱挽歌。

translations.literal: Wenlüe played pipa and blew the transverse flute, sang ballads, and when weary would lie down and intone dirges.
translations.idiomatic: In prison he played pipa and flute, sang songs, and when tired would lie down and chant dirges.

sentences.zh: 居數月，奪防者弓矢以射人曰：「不然，天子不憶我。

translations.literal: After several months he seized his guards’ bow and arrows and shot at people, saying, “Otherwise the Son of Heaven would not remember me.”
translations.idiomatic: After months in custody he seized his guards’ bow and shot at people, crying, “Otherwise the emperor would never think of me.”

sentences.zh: 」有司奏之，伏法。

translations.literal: The authorities reported this, and he was executed.
translations.idiomatic: Officials reported him, and he was put to death.

sentences.zh: 文略嘗大遺魏收金，請為其父作佳傳，收論尒朱榮比韋、彭、伊、霍，蓋由是也。

translations.literal: Wenlüe once gave Wei Shou a large gift of gold and asked him to write a fine biography of his father; that Wei Shou compared Erzhu Rong to Wei Qing, Peng Yue, Yi Yin, and Huo Guang was largely for this reason.
translations.idiomatic: Wenlüe once paid Wei Shou heavily to glorify his father in print—hence Shou’s likening of Erzhu Rong to Wei Qing, Peng Yue, Yi Yin, and Huo Guang.

sentences.zh: 鄭仲禮，滎陽開封人，魏鴻臚嚴庶子也。

translations.literal: Zheng Zhongli was a native of Kaifeng in Xingyang; he was the son of Yan, Director of Ceremonial of Wei.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng Zhongli was from Kaifeng in Xingyang, son of Yan, Wei’s director of ceremonial.

sentences.zh: 少輕險，有膂力，高祖嬖寵其姊，以親戚被昵，擢帳內都督。

translations.literal: In youth he was reckless and had physical strength; Gaozu favored his elder sister, and as a kinsman he was treated with intimacy and promoted to commander in the personal guard.
translations.idiomatic: Young and reckless, strong of body, he rose through Gaozu’s fondness for his sister to a post in the personal guard.

sentences.zh: 嘗執高祖弓刀，出入隨從。

translations.literal: He once carried Gaozu’s bow and blade and attended him in and out.
translations.idiomatic: He even bore Gaozu’s bow and sword and attended him everywhere.

sentences.zh: 任胄為好酒不憂公事，高祖責之，胄懼，謀為逆。

translations.literal: Ren Zhou loved wine and neglected official business; Gaozu reproved him, and in fear Zhou plotted rebellion.
translations.idiomatic: Ren Zhou drank and neglected duty; rebuked by Gaozu, he turned to treason.

sentences.zh: 賴武明婁後為請，故仲禮死，不及其家。

translations.literal: Thanks to Empress Wuming Lou’s intercession, Zhongli alone was put to death and his family was not implicated.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Wuming Lou pleaded for him, so only Zhongli died and his kin were spared.

sentences.zh: 李祖升，趙國平棘人，顯祖李皇後之長兄。

translations.literal: Li Zusheng was a native of Pingji in Zhao Commandery and the eldest brother of Empress Li of Emperor Xianzu.
translations.idiomatic: Li Zusheng was from Pingji in Zhao and the elder brother of Xianzu’s Empress Li.

sentences.zh: 父希宗，上黨守。

translations.literal: His father Xizong was Administrator of Shangdang.
translations.idiomatic: His father Xizong had been administrator of Shangdang.

sentences.zh: 祖升儀容瑰麗，垂手過膝，睦姻好施，文學足以自通。

translations.literal: Zusheng’s bearing was splendid; his hands hung below his knees. He was kind in kinship and generous in giving, and his literary learning sufficed for ordinary intercourse.
translations.idiomatic: Handsome and open-handed, with hands reaching past his knees, he was gracious to kin and literate enough for polite society.

sentences.zh: 仕至齊州刺史，為徒兵所害。

translations.literal: He rose to Inspector of Qi Province and was killed by conscript soldiers.
translations.idiomatic: He reached the post of Qi inspector before conscript soldiers killed him.

sentences.zh: 弟祖勳，顯祖受禪，除秘書丞。

translations.literal: His younger brother Zuxun, when Xianzu received the abdication, was appointed Secretary of the Palace Library.
translations.idiomatic: Younger brother Zuxun became palace librarian when Xianzu took the throne.

sentences.zh: 及女為濟南王妃，除侍中，封丹陽王。

translations.literal: When his daughter became consort to the Prince of Jinan, he was made Palace Attendant and enfeoffed Prince of Danyang.
translations.idiomatic: When his daughter married the Prince of Jinan, he was made palace attendant and prince of Danyang.

sentences.zh: 濟南廢，為光州刺史。

translations.literal: After Jinan was deposed, he was made Inspector of Guang Province.
translations.idiomatic: After Jinan’s deposition he was sent to Guang as inspector.

sentences.zh: 祖勳性貪慢，兼妻崔氏驕豪干政，時論鄙之。

translations.literal: Zuxun was greedy and arrogant, and his wife of the Cui clan was overbearing and meddled in government; contemporary opinion despised them.
translations.idiomatic: Greedy and arrogant, with a domineering Cui wife who meddled in affairs, he was widely scorned.

sentences.zh: 以數坐贓免官。

translations.literal: He was repeatedly dismissed from office for corruption.
translations.idiomatic: Repeated corruption charges cost him his posts.

sentences.zh: 無才幹，自少及長，居官皆因內寵，無可稱述，卒。

translations.literal: He had no talent; from youth to old age his offices all came through palace favor, and there is nothing worth recounting—he died.
translations.idiomatic: Without talent he held office only through court favor; nothing in his career merits praise—he simply died.

sentences.zh: 元蠻，魏太師江陽王繼子，肅宗元皇後之父也。

translations.literal: Yuan Man was the adopted son of Yuan Ji, Grand Tutor and Prince of Jiangyang in Wei, and the father of Empress Yuan of Emperor Suzong.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Man was the adopted son of Wei Grand Tutor Prince Jiangyang Ji and father of Suzong’s Empress Yuan.

sentences.zh: 歷光祿卿。

translations.literal: He served successively as Director of the Imperial Household.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to director of the imperial household.

sentences.zh: 天保十年，大誅元氏，肅宗為蠻苦請，因是追原之，賜姓步六孤氏。

translations.literal: In the tenth year of Tianbao there was a great slaughter of the Yuan clan; Suzong pleaded bitterly for Man and he was therefore pardoned and granted the surname Buliugu.
translations.idiomatic: In Tianbao year ten, when the Yuan were massacred, Suzong’s pleas won Man a pardon and the surname Buliugu.

sentences.zh: 尋病卒。

translations.literal: Shortly afterward he died of illness.
translations.idiomatic: He soon died of illness.

sentences.zh: 胡長仁，字孝隆，安定臨涇人，武成皇後之兄。

translations.literal: Hu Changren, courtesy name Xiaolong, was a native of Linjing in Anding and elder brother of Empress Hu of Emperor Wucheng.
translations.idiomatic: Hu Changren, styled Xiaolong, was from Linjing in Anding and elder brother of Wucheng’s Empress Hu.

sentences.zh: 父延之，魏中書令。

translations.literal: His father Yanzhi was Secretariat Director in Wei.
translations.idiomatic: His father Yanzhi had been Wei’s secretariat director.

sentences.zh: 長仁累遷右樸射及尚書令。

translations.literal: Changren was repeatedly promoted to Right Vice Director of the Masters of Writing and Director of the Department of State Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Changren rose to right vice director of the Masters of Writing and director of the Department of State Affairs.

sentences.zh: 世祖崩，預參朝政，封隴東王。

translations.literal: When Emperor Shizu died, he took part in deliberating government and was enfeoffed Prince of Longdong.
translations.idiomatic: At Shizu’s death he joined in governing and was made prince of Longdong.

sentences.zh: 左丞鄒孝裕、郎中陸仁惠、盧元亮厚相結托。

translations.literal: Left Assistant Zou Xiaoyu and Gentlemen of the Palace Lu Renhui and Lu Yuanliang formed a close, trusting bond with him.
translations.idiomatic: Left assistant Zou Xiaoyu and gentlemen Lu Renhui and Lu Yuanliang attached themselves to him.

sentences.zh: 長仁每上省，孝裕必方駕而來。

translations.literal: Whenever Changren went up to the provincial offices, Xiaoyu would certainly come in parallel carriages.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever Changren entered the provincial offices, Xiaoyu arrived in a matching carriage.

sentences.zh: 省務既繁，簿案堆積，令史欲諮都座者日有百數。

translations.literal: Provincial business was already heavy and documents piled up; clerks wishing to consult the chief seat numbered a hundred or more each day.
translations.idiomatic: Paperwork overwhelmed the offices; a hundred clerks a day might seek the chief seat.

sentences.zh: 孝裕屏人私話，朝退亦相隨，仁惠、元亮又伺間而往，停斷公事，時人號為三佞。

translations.literal: Xiaoyu would dismiss others for private talk; after court he would follow along as well, and Renhui and Yuanliang would seize intervals to go too, halting public business—people of the time called them the Three Flatterers.
translations.idiomatic: Xiaoyu drew him aside for private talk and followed him from court; Renhui and Yuanliang slipped in between sessions and stalled the bureaucracy—contemporaries dubbed them the Three Flatterers.

sentences.zh: 長仁私遊密席，處處追尋。

translations.literal: Changren’s private feasts and secret gatherings were pursued and tracked everywhere.
translations.idiomatic: His secret feasts and private parties were notorious.

sentences.zh: 孝裕勸其求進，和士開深疾之，於是奏除孝裕為章武郡守，元亮等皆出。

translations.literal: Xiaoyu urged him to seek advancement; He Shikai deeply hated this, and therefore memorialized to remove Xiaoyu as Administrator of Zhangwu Commandery and to send Yuanliang and the others out as well.
translations.idiomatic: Xiaoyu urged him to climb higher; He Shikai, loathing this, had Xiaoyu sent to Zhangwu and the others posted away.

sentences.zh: 孝裕又說長仁曰：「王陽臥疾，士開必來，因而殺之。

translations.literal: Xiaoyu again said to Changren, “If the prince feigns illness, Shikai will certainly come, and you can kill him then.
translations.idiomatic: Xiaoyu told Changren, “Feign illness—when Shikai comes, kill him.

sentences.zh: 入見太后，不過百日失官，便代其處。

translations.literal: Go in to see the empress dowager; within no more than a hundred days you will lose office, then take his place.”
translations.idiomatic: See the empress dowager; within a hundred days you lose your post, then you take his.”

sentences.zh: 」士開知謀，徙孝裕為北營州建德郡守。

translations.literal: Shikai learned of the plot and transferred Xiaoyu to be Administrator of Jiande Commandery in North Ying Province.
translations.idiomatic: Shikai uncovered the plot and sent Xiaoyu to Jiande in North Ying Province.

sentences.zh: 後長仁倚親，驕豪無畏憚。

translations.literal: Later Changren, relying on his kinship, was arrogant and feared nothing.
translations.idiomatic: Later, secure in his kinship, Changren grew arrogant and fearless.

sentences.zh: 士開出為齊州刺史。

translations.literal: Shikai went out to serve as Inspector of Qi Province.
translations.idiomatic: Shikai left the capital to be inspector of Qi Province.

sentences.zh: 長仁怨憤，謀令剌士開，事覺，遂賜死。

translations.literal: Changren, resentful and angry, plotted to have Shikai assassinated; the affair was discovered and he was ordered to die.
translations.idiomatic: Changren, bitter, plotted assassination; discovered, he was ordered to take his own life.

sentences.zh: 尋而後主納長仁女為后，重加贈謚，長仁弟等前後七人並賜王爵，合門貴盛。

translations.literal: Soon afterward the Later Lord took Changren’s daughter as empress and richly added posthumous honors; Changren’s younger brothers and others, seven in all before and after, were granted princely titles, and the whole household flourished in glory.
translations.idiomatic: Soon the Later Lord married Changren’s daughter; honors were heaped on the dead, and seven brothers in all were made princes—the clan blazed with rank.

sentences.zh: 全文以中華書局、一九七二年十一月、第一版《北齊書》為本校。

translations.literal: The full text has been collated against the first edition of the Book of Northern Qi published by Zhonghua Book Company in November 1972.
translations.idiomatic: This text has been collated against the Zhonghua Book Company first edition of the Book of Northern Qi (November 1972).
